questions.q: List the three categories of extension teaching methods based on the number of learners and interaction intensity.
questions.a: The three categories are individual contact methods, group contact methods, and mass contact methods. A wrong answer (e.g., listing "lecture, demonstration, field day" without categorising) reveals the student is confusing specific methods with the overarching classification framework. The classification is the mental scaffold; specific methods are instances.

questions.q: Explain why individual contact methods are more effective for skill development but less efficient for reaching large numbers.
questions.a: Individual methods (farm visit, office call) allow tailored pacing, immediate feedback, and hands-on guided practice — essential for psychomotor skills. However, they require high worker time per learner, making them impractical for large audiences. A wrong answer that claims "individual methods reach more people because they are personal" confuses effectiveness per learner with overall reach.

questions.q: A KVK scientist wants to teach 500 farmers about pest identification. Choose the most appropriate method category and justify your choice in two sentences.
questions.a: Mass contact methods (e.g., radio programme, poster exhibition, SMS alerts) are most appropriate because the audience is large and geographically dispersed, and the learning objective is awareness/knowledge of pest identification — not a complex psychomotor skill. A wrong choice of group or individual method ignores the resource constraint: 500 farmers cannot be accommodated in feasible group sessions or individual visits within a reasonable time.

questions.q: Compare group discussion and method demonstration in terms of learner participation, cost, and suitability for attitude change.
questions.a: Group discussion: high participation (verbal), low cost, excellent for attitude change through peer exchange. Method demonstration: moderate participation (observation + practice), moderate cost (materials), good for skill acquisition but weaker for attitude change. A wrong answer that rates both equally on all dimensions fails to distinguish the cognitive (discussion) vs psychomotor (demonstration) focus of each method.

questions.q: Critique the statement: "Mass contact methods are obsolete in the digital age because everyone has smartphones."
questions.a: The statement is flawed. First, smartphone penetration is not universal — digital divide excludes marginalised groups (women, elderly, remote areas). Second, mass contact includes non-digital methods (wall paintings, folk media) that work without connectivity. Third, even digital mass methods (YouTube, WhatsApp) lack interaction for skill practice and trust-building. A wrong answer agreeing with the statement shows ignorance of the digital divide and the unique strengths of non-digital mass methods.

questions.q: Design a combined extension teaching strategy for promoting kitchen gardening in an urban slum, using at least one method from each category (individual, group, mass).
questions.a: Mass: Community radio spots + poster on "Grow your own vegetables" in local language. Group: Method demonstration of container gardening at the anganwadi centre with 15 women per batch. Individual: Follow-up home visits to troubleshoot each family's containers, advise on watering, pest control. A poor answer lists three methods but does not sequence them logically (mass → awareness, group → skill, individual → adoption support) or ignores the slum context (space constraints, water scarcity).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Extension teaching methods are systematic approaches used by extension workers to disseminate information, skills, and ______ to target audiences, classified into individual contact (one-to-one), group contact (small groups), and mass contact (large audiences) methods based on the number of learners and interaction intensity.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are an ______ worker in a village where farmers need to learn a new organic composting technique.
What is Extension teaching methods? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Extension teaching methods are systematic approaches used by extension workers to disseminate information, skills, and technologies to target audiences, classified into individual contact (one-to-one), group contact (small groups), and mass contact (large audiences) methods based on the number of learners and interaction intensity.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Extension teaching methods?
questions.a: Students often think that mass contact methods (TV, radio, WhatsApp) are "better" because they reach more people, but they ignore that these methods are poor for complex skill transfer and sustained behaviour change.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can classify any given extension teaching method into individual, group, or mass contact category, justify the selection of a method for a specific extension situation, and explain the advantages and limitations of each category.
